items.claim: The dent-growth criterion is this seat's derivation: the face's fixed membrane force pR/4 on a paraboloid dent's curvature, against the core's crush strength less its share of the pressure, with the patch's plate buckling force taken off. No opened page prints it. Castanie, the CAI literature on face wrinkling over crushed core, and McGowan and Ambur's preload threshold support the mechanism, not the numbers.
items.needed_to_ground: Compression-after-impact tests on beryllium-faced CR-III coupons at 300 MPa, dented at 0.25-2 mm over 30-100 mm.

items.claim: The lost-core patch is read clamped (54.8 mm) and simply supported (27.1 mm); the real edge, a face continuous over intact core, lies between. The pressure that holds the face on the crushed core is a barrier this static reading ignores.
items.needed_to_ground: A plate-on-crushable-foundation analysis of the dented patch, or the coupon test above.

items.claim: The dent model (face membrane plus core crush over a plastic spread) is this seat's. It reads Pach's test within its 1.1-1.2 mm and 30 mm, and Clarke's FE at about half the FE depth. Hail is read three ways (fluid, Shi-calibrated, all energy) that span ten times in depth.
items.needed_to_ground: Ice-ball tests on a beryllium-faced CR-III panel at 25-75 mm and IEC velocities.

items.claim: No impact, puncture or through-thickness ductility data exist for thin SR-200 sheet. NASA 1971 calls beryllium's impact resistance extremely low. A cracked outer face vents its core cells; whether the CR-III core is perforated (034's evacuation of every cell) decides whether a crack vents the whole core.
items.needed_to_ground: Drop and ice-ball tests on 0.8 mm SR-200 sheet over honeycomb, and the core venting design.

items.claim: Each dent is scored alone against gamma 0.564; the as-built imperfection already spends that allowance, so a dent and the as-built shape compete for it.
items.needed_to_ground: 015's map with two interacting imperfections, or a measured shell.

items.claim: No hail flux (stones per square metre per storm, by size) was sourced, so the number of tube strikes in a storm is not given.
items.needed_to_ground: A hail climatology for the site.

items.claim: The tube's hail stress uses a shallow-shell-on-foundation reading of a cylinder, a static contact pressure (fluid or Shi-calibrated), no dynamic amplification, and the 14 mm Hexoloy tube data without size scaling. Birds, timber debris and tool drops on the tubes are not scored. No SiC tube impact test was found.
items.needed_to_ground: Ice-ball tests on a 275 mm, 1.14 mm-wall SiC tube.

items.claim: No Zylon/PBO film exists as a sourced product: no modulus, toughness, puncture or tear data. The tear lengths use other films' toughness and a projected modulus. The film is also unprotected from daylight (35 percent strength after six months).
items.needed_to_ground: A built 0/90 PBO film with barrier, tested for puncture, slit tear under biaxial load and UV.

items.claim: The lost-member screen is linear, rigid-jointed, on f4/f5 geodesics not at 022d's spacing, with lumped pressure loads; joint stiffness is unknown and no nonlinear collapse was run. 026b's discrete model is the place to repeat it.
items.needed_to_ground: A nonlinear frame analysis with one member removed, on 026b's model with the real joint stiffness.

items.claim: The film over the two bays a lost member leaves is scored at the same rise-to-span, a tension 1.5 times higher; the real film shape after loss is not modelled.
items.needed_to_ground: A membrane analysis of the rhombic bay.

items.claim: The descent model is a rigid sphere in ISA with an isothermal fill, a constant drag coefficient 0.2-0.47, added mass 0.5 rho V and no wind; the neutral-buoyancy pressure result assumes the inside air takes the outside temperature.
items.needed_to_ground: A coupled thermal and trajectory model, and the site's atmosphere.

items.claim: At a hole the face reads twice its membrane stress and yields out to 3.9 hole radii; whether the edge crumples and the hole grows while the slow leak keeps the load on is not modelled.
items.needed_to_ground: A hole-edge analysis of the sandwich at 300 MPa, or a punctured coupon under biaxial compression.

items.claim: No mast contact speed was sourced; TAR 473 and 14 CFR 25.473 stand in, and the 0.5 m contact patch is assumed.
items.needed_to_ground: A mooring system design and its contact envelope.

items.claim: 14 CFR 101.13 limits moored balloons to 152.4 m above the surface, below the 500 m design point; 101.19 requires a rapid-deflation device, which for a vacuum hull is a rapid air valve that lands it heavy.
items.needed_to_ground: A regulatory route for a 500 m moored or free vacuum hull.

items.claim: No inspection limit was sourced for beryllium faces, SiC tubes or PBO film; the tap-test PoD is for 0.5 mm aluminium and falls with face thickness. Access to a 1257 m2 hull at 500 m is not addressed.
items.needed_to_ground: PoD trials on beryllium-faced coupons and an inspection-robot concept.

items.claim: Bird and hail readings disagree by reading: a moored 4 lb bird is stable on the fluid pressure and grows on the all-energy reading.
items.needed_to_ground: Soft-body impact analysis on the sandwich.
